name: litellm-vscode-chat
displayName: LiteLLM Provider for GitHub Copilot Chat
description: An extension that integrates LiteLLM into GitHub Copilot Chat

apiKey.title: API Key
apiKey.description: LiteLLM API key. Leave empty for servers without authentication.

oauthTokenUrl.title: OAuth Token URL
oauthTokenUrl.description: OAuth2 token endpoint for client-credentials authentication, e.g. https://idp.example.com/oauth2/token. Set this together with the client ID to authenticate with a short-lived bearer token instead of a static API key.

oauthClientId.title: OAuth Client ID
oauthClientId.description: Client ID for the OAuth2 client-credentials grant. Required together with the token URL.

oauthClientSecret.title: OAuth Client Secret
oauthClientSecret.description: Client secret for the OAuth2 client-credentials grant. Leave empty for public clients.

oauthScopes.title: OAuth Scopes
oauthScopes.description: Space-separated scopes to request with the token, e.g. "litellm.read litellm.write". Leave empty to request none.

virtualKeyHeader.title: Virtual Key Header
virtualKeyHeader.description: Name of a custom header carrying a LiteLLM virtual key, e.g. x-litellm-api-key. Sent on every request to this server when both the header and its value are set.

virtualKeyValue.title: Virtual Key Value
virtualKeyValue.description: The virtual key sent in the header named above.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with LiteLLM for Copilot Chat
walkthroughs.description: Connect a LiteLLM server and use its models in GitHub Copilot Chat.

steps.title: Connect your LiteLLM server
steps.description:
Add your server in VS Code's Manage Language Models editor: pick LiteLLM as the provider, then enter the base URL and, if your server needs one, an API key.
[Open Manage Language Models](command:workbench.action.chat.manage)

steps.title: Pick a LiteLLM model in chat
steps.description:
Open Copilot Chat and click the model picker at the bottom of the chat input. Models from your LiteLLM server are listed under the name you gave it.
[Open Copilot Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)

steps.title: Configure per-model options
steps.description: Select a LiteLLM model that supports reasoning, then click the "Thinking Effort" label next to the model name in the chat input. "Provider default" sends nothing and leaves the choice to your provider.

steps.title: Verify the connection
steps.description:
Run a connection test to check every configured server and count the models it serves.
[Test Connection](command:litellm.testConnection)

steps.title: Fine-tune the extension
steps.description:
Timeouts, model list caching, prompt caching, custom headers, and per-model request parameters live in the extension settings.
[Open Settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22@ext:vivswan.litellm-vscode-chat%22%5D)

litellm-vscode-chat.servers.markdownDescription: LiteLLM servers, declared as settings. Machine-scoped: this lives in your user settings only (workspaces cannot override it, and Settings Sync does not carry it to other machines). Each entry syncs to a VS Code language-model provider group automatically, so servers can be managed here or in the LiteLLM dashboard without touching the native editor. The `label` is the entry's identity: renaming it creates a new provider group, and removing an entry cannot remove its group (VS Code offers no API for that; use the native Manage Language Models editor). Secret fields (`apiKey`, `oauthClientSecret`, `virtualKeyValue`) may be written inline here - visible in settings files - or omitted and stored in VS Code secret storage instead, via the dashboard or the 'LiteLLM: Set Server Secret' command. Inline values take precedence over stored ones.

label.description: Display name and identity of the server; the provider group is named after it.

apiKey.description: LiteLLM API key, inline. Omit to keep it in secret storage instead, or for servers without authentication.

oauthTokenUrl.description: OAuth2 token endpoint for client-credentials authentication. Set together with the client ID.

oauthClientId.description: Client ID for the OAuth2 client-credentials grant. Required together with the token URL.

oauthClientSecret.description: OAuth client secret, inline. Omit to keep it in secret storage instead, or for public clients.

oauthScopes.description: Space-separated scopes to request with the token. Leave out to request none.

virtualKeyHeader.description: Name of a custom header carrying a LiteLLM virtual key, e.g. x-litellm-api-key.

virtualKeyValue.description: The virtual key sent in the header named above, inline. Omit to keep it in secret storage instead.

litellm-vscode-chat.defaultMaxOutputToke.description: Default maximum output tokens when not provided by model info

litellm-vscode-chat.defaultContextLength.description: Default context length when not provided by model info

litellm-vscode-chat.defaultMaxInputToken.description: Default maximum input tokens (if null, calculated as contextLength - maxOutputTokens)

litellm-vscode-chat.promptCaching.enable.description: Enable prompt caching for supported models (currently Anthropic Claude). Places cache breakpoints on the tool definitions, the system prompt, the first user message, and the last text-bearing message of the conversation, so agent sessions reuse the cached prefix instead of re-paying for the whole history every turn. Only affects models that advertise prompt caching support.

litellm-vscode-chat.modelParameters.description: Model-specific request parameters to customize API behavior. Supports max_tokens, temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, stop, etc. Uses longest prefix matching (e.g., 'gpt-4' matches 'gpt-4-turbo:openai'). To scope parameters to a specific server, prefix with the server's base URL (e.g., 'http://localhost:4000/gpt-4') or, for servers configured before the provider-group migration, the server label (e.g., 'Production/gpt-4'). Server-scoped entries take priority over unscoped ones. Only parameters you set are sent; the extension never injects defaults.

litellm-vscode-chat.headers.description: Custom HTTP headers to include with all LiteLLM requests (model discovery and chat completions). Useful for API gateways that require headers like x-litellm-api-key. If values contain secrets, prefer User settings (not workspace settings) to avoid accidental commits.

litellm-vscode-chat.maskApiKeyInput.description: Mask the API key input field when configuring. Disable to see the key as you type.

litellm-vscode-chat.requestTimeout.description: Request timeout in milliseconds for chat completion requests. Default is 300000ms (5 minutes). Increase this value if you're experiencing timeout errors with long-running requests.

litellm-vscode-chat.discoveryTimeout.description: Request timeout in milliseconds for model discovery requests. Default is 30000ms (30 seconds).

litellm-vscode-chat.discoveryCacheTtl.description: How long, in milliseconds, discovered model lists are reused before the server is asked again. Default is 3600000 (1 hour). Higher values avoid repeated discovery requests when VS Code re-resolves providers in bursts, but models added or removed on the server take up to this long to appear; lower values pick up server-side changes sooner at the cost of more requests. Set to 0 to ask the server on every refresh (simultaneous refreshes still share one request). Run 'LiteLLM: Sync Models Now' to refresh immediately regardless of this setting.

scripts.test: bun run compile && bun run bundle:dev && vscode-test --label unit
scripts.test:coverage: bun run compile && bun run bundle:dev && vscode-test --label unit --coverage && bun scripts/check-coverage.ts
